name: person
description: Someone, by name, with the colour they have everywhere in the workspace: who a record is for, who is here, who changed something.

use.when: a person is named beside what concerns them: who a task is for, who else is here.
use.not: a link to their page (use link), or a word that is not a person.
use.with: record and collection, where a record is for someone; presence.

name.description: What the person is called, in full, as they write it. Never cut short: a long name wraps, and a name in a script written right to left keeps its own direction.

colour.description: Their colour, 1 to 6, the same on every computer (chat.PersonColour of their login). Left out, the dot is neutral.

label.description: Words before the name, such as For, so the chip reads For Hana.

wcag.notes: The name is the meaning; the dot is aria-hidden decoration, so no one needs to tell colours apart (1.4.1), and as a supplementary mark it is not held to 1.4.11, though the six colours stand 3:1 on the page anyway. The name keeps the text colour at full contrast; the six colours are for marks, not text. The name sits in bdi, so a right-to-left name does not reorder the words and punctuation around it. The chip is inline and breaks anywhere, so a long name wraps at 320px (1.4.10). A proper name needs no lang (3.1.2). In forced colours every dot is CanvasText and the name says who.

machine.identify: The text is the label and the name; the name alone is the bdi. data-person is their colour, 1 to 6.
